subStrands.name: Percussion Musical Instruments (Drawing)
content: Identifying: name, community, method of playing
Making charcoal sticks (cutting, trimming, burning, cooling)

outcomes.text: identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities
classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic
discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument
improvise rhythmic patterns using indigenous percussion musical instruments
make charcoal sticks for drawing
create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion instrument using the smudging technique
appreciate indigenous percussion instruments from Kenyan communities and pictures drawn

learningExperiences: watch virtual or actual percussion musical instruments to identify by; name, community and method of playing
observe/listen to sounds of percussion musical instruments and classify as melodic or non- melodic
identify parts of a percussion musical instrument and discuss their function(s) in sound production
practice improvising rhythmic patterns to accompany songs using percussion instruments
talk about value/ tone as an element of art created on virtual and actual sample pictures
collaboratively, collect materials and tools to make charcoal sticks following the correct procedure while observing safety
use charcoal sticks to illustrate how to create tone/value by smudging technique
draw using charcoal sticks a picture of one percussion instrument and create tonal variation by smudging technique
show and talk about own and peers’ percussion instruments and drawings in a just and fair manner
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the importance of percussion instruments from different communities in Kenya?
How is tonal variation created in a drawing?
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: the learner speaks clearly and listens keenly while discussing about parts of a percussion instrument and their roles.
Digital literacy: the learner interacts with digital devices to source information on percussion instruments.
values: Social justice: the learner talks about own and others’ pictures justly.
Responsibility: the learner cares for own and peers’ items and observes safety precautions when making charcoal sticks.
pcis: Social Cohesion: the learner acquires skill of working with others while making charcoal sticks in groups.
Safety and security: the learner observes fire safety when burning charcoal sticks.
Environmental conservation: the learner conserves the environment by carefully collecting materials for making a charcoal sticks.
links: Social Studies: the learner exploits natural resources responsibly to make charcoal sticks.

subStrands.name: Netball

outcomes.text: discuss the skills of passing and catching in Netball
make a ball using macramé technique
perform the skills of passing, and catching in Netball
appreciate Netball as a team game for enjoyment

learningExperiences: watch a virtual or live Netball game and identify passes and catching skills
demonstrate passing (chest and overhead) and catching (double- handed) skills
collect reusable materials and improvise balls using macramé technique (overhand knot)
practise passing (chest and overhead) and catching (double- handed) skills
play a Mini-Netball game applying the skills of (passing and catching) while observing safety
talk about own and others’ skills in Netball game
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are the skills of passing and catching important in a Netball game?
Why is it necessary to improvise a netball?
coreCompetencies: Creativity and Imagination: The learner explores varied materials when improvising balls.
Learning to learn: The learner watches a Netball game to learn the netball skills through demonstration and practise.
values: Social justice: The learner demonstrates fairness as they take turns in practising the netball skills of shooting, catching and passing.
Responsibility: The learner takes the initiative to clean the working area and store the balls in an improvised storage.
Unity: the learner works together with peers when painting, improvising a ball and performing the Netball skills of catching and passing.
pcis: Resource mobilisation and utilisation: The learner collects locally available materials to improvise a netball.
Self-esteem: The learner displays confidence in demonstrating new skills through practice and playing a Netball game.
links: Mathematics: The learner takes part in passing the Netball to a team-mate while applying ball trajectory visualisation.

subStrands.name: Painting and Montage

outcomes.text: classify colours into primary and secondary for painting
paint a picture for colour value application
create a montage composition for expression
appreciate painting and montage as methods of making pictures

learningExperiences: mix primary colours to create secondary colours
mix white with a secondary colour to create light tones on a scale strip
mix black with a secondary colour to create dark tones on a scale strip
draw a single object and paint with emphasis on colour value
observe sample montage pictures for familiarity
source picture of ball games and cut out
arrange and paste cut-out pictures to make a montage themed “ball games” and clean the working area
show and take turns to talk about their own and others work
keyInquiryQuestions: How is glue for pasting pictures improvised?
Why is colour classification important in painting?
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly about their own and others work.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner makes thoughtful choices when producing a montage pictorial composition.
values: Respect: The learner accommodates others’ views during critique of their own and others’ painting and montage work.
Love: The learner takes turns to talk about their own and others work.
pcis: Social Cohesion: The learner acquires the skill of working with others during creating a montage composition.
links: Mathematics: The learner mixes colours in correct proportions to classify as primary or secondary colours.

subStrands.name: Rhythm
content: Note values: crotchet, pair of quavers and their rests
Note symbols: crochet, a pair of quavers and their rests
Qualities: Variation of note values, repetition of patterns, ending on a long note

outcomes.text: interpret rhythmic patterns involving the crotchet, pair of quaver and their rests
write the French rhythm taa and ta-te, names using free hand lettering
describe the qualities of a good rhythmic pattern
compose a rhythmic pattern involving a crochet, a pair of quavers and their rests
enjoy creating rhythmic patterns

learningExperiences: listen to/sing familiar topical songs and identify the music notes and their rests using their French rhythm names
clap the rhythm of the songs while reciting their rhythms using French rhythm names
write letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand lettering- ascenders and descenders
use free hand lettering to write French rhythm names taa and ta-te
relate the French rhythm names taa, and ta-te to music note symbols for crotchet and a pair of quavers
practice writing the note symbols; crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests on monotone
discuss the techniques used in composing rhythmic patterns
write rhythmic patterns from dictation using either French rhythm names or note symbols and their rests
compose original rhythmic patterns and write them using French rhythm names and note symbols and their rests
critique rhythms created by self and peers respecting each other’s views
keyInquiryQuestions: How can a rhythm be created?
coreCompetencies: Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly during critique of own and others’ rhythms.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner composes original rhythmic patterns and writes them using French rhythm names, note symbols and their rests.
values: Respect: The learner accommodates others’ views during critique of own and others’ original rhythmic compositions.
Integrity: The learner creates own original rhythmic patterns.
pcis: Social Cohesion: The learner acquires the skill of working with others during group composition of rhythmic patterns.
Social Justice: The learner fairly critiques rhythms created by others and self.
links: English: The learner applies the concept of syllabic division in reciting French rhythm names of words and writing letters of the alphabet in lowercase using free hand.
Mathematics: The learner uses the concept of numbers when relating the value of the quaver in relation to the crotchet.

subStrands.name: Melody
content: Kodaly hand signs for d r m
Qualities of a melody; use of stepwise motion, variation of the sol-fa syllables and sound duration, ending on d

outcomes.text: identify sol-fa syllables d r m in a simple melody
interpret hand signs for the sol-fa syllables d r m for pitch discrimination
state the qualities of a good melody as a foundation to composition
create short melodies using the sol-fa syllables d, r and m
model clay slabs with sol-fa syllables using coil and slab techniques
enjoy creating short melodies and modelling using clay

learningExperiences: sing familiar songs based on the sol-fa syllables d r m, and identify the sol-fa syllables by ear
listen to and identify aurally and orally the sol-fa pitches (d r m) as sounded on a melodic instrument/voice
watch videos/demonstrations of execution of the Kodaly hand signs for the sol-fa syllables d, r m and practise performing the hand signs
brainstorm on the qualities of a good melody
apply composition techniques to create short melodies based on the sol-fa syllables d r m and the note symbols; crotchet, a pair of quavers and their rests
collect clay for modelling from the local environment
roll clay into slab and cut out three rectangular pieces of three different sizes
model so-lfa syllables (d r m) using coil technique and attach on the slabs
keyInquiryQuestions: How can interesting melodies be created?
coreCompetencies: Creativity and Imagination: The learner uses unique and new ideas to compose melodies and models the sol-fa syllables.
Self-efficacy: The learner models the sol-fa syllables and composes original melodies.
values: Unity: The learner works with peers when modelling, creating and performing various melodies.
Love: The learner respects others while critiquing their performances.
pcis: Life skills: The learner acquires interpersonal skills through interacting with peers in groups as they model sol-fa syllables and create melodies.
Mentorship and peer education: The learner shares their compositions with peers who give feedback for improvement.
links: Mathematics: The learner applies the skill of sequencing of sol-fa syllables when creating simple melodies using stepwise motion.
